prerequisites: Differential equations resolution and Fourier and Laplace transform applications.
Fundamental elements of electrical engineering knowledge.
Fundamentals of automatic knowledge (Bode diagrams, Feedback).

learning_outcomes.text: Provide the student with the basics for the analysis of elementary electronic circuits, both analog and digital.
Introduce the characteristics of basic electronic devices: diode, MOS transistor and bipolar transistor.
Study the applications of basic electronic devices in logic circuits and in amplifiers.

syllabus_topics: Ideal operational amplifier: definition, characteristics, inverting and non-inverting configuration
Voltage-current characteristic: the forward bias region, the reverse bias region, the breakdown region
Models of the direct characteristic of the diode
Model for small signals and related applications
Rectifier circuits: single half-wave rectifier, double half-wave rectifier, bridge rectifier, single half-wave precision rectifier (super diode)
Structure and physical functioning of the enrichment and depletion MOSFET
Voltage-current characteristics: circuit symbols and graphic representations of the characteristics of MOSFETs
Polarization of a MOS amplifier circuit
Fundamental configurations of MOSFET amplifiers with resistive and active load
Fundamentals of digital electronics: logic inverter as a fundamental binary element
Transfer characteristic of a logic inverter
Moore's law: integrated circuits integration scales
Silicon: main material in electronic and optical devices
Processes for manufacturing the P-N junction
Capacity and tracing of the MOS device
Noise margins and minimization of the inverter area
Circuit capacity, dynamic analysis and propagation times
CMOS Inverter, Transfer Characteristics and Noise Margins
Fan-in and Fan-out of the CMOS ports
assessment_rules: The assessment is through an oral interview. Evaluation criteria include maturity on course content, quality of oral exposure, critical spirit, judgment autonomy, and mastery of scientific language. The oral exam may include discussion of classroom exercises and laboratory projects, which the student will present. The final grade, expressed out of thirty, is based on the achievement of these criteria. Praise may be awarded for an oral test that fully satisfies the evaluation criteria.
